summary.headline: AU SFB Q2 FY27 PAT up 53% YoY to INR858 Cr; deposits up 29% YoY, GNPA down to 1.99%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed strong balance-sheet growth, with deposits up 29% YoY and loans up 25% YoY, and PAT rising 53% YoY to INR858 Cr. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 1.99% and credit cost including guarantee premium at 0.8%, driven by unsecured normalisation. NIM fell 9 bps QoQ to 5.8% on higher investment book and seasonality, and management flagged cost-of-funds and yield pressure from the 25 bps repo hike. Management reiterated the ~90 bps credit cost guidance and said nothing is visible yet in October collections, though the insurance fee consultation is a medium-term ROA headwind.

segments.name: Branch Banking (deposits)
segments.commentary: Accounts for 61% of total deposits; current account balances up 55% YoY (61% on daily average) and savings account balances up 23% YoY.

segments.name: Wheels
segments.commentary: Book crossed INR50,000 Cr, reaching about INR51,000 Cr; up 27% YoY and 6% QoQ on new-vehicle demand and new geographies.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Grew 102% YoY and 4% QoQ to about INR4,700 Cr; portfolio LTV about 75%; QoQ moderation attributed to lower gold prices reducing renewals and balance transfers.

segments.name: Mortgages (MBL + affordable housing)
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY and 2% QoQ; MBL disbursements up 17% YoY; affordable housing deliberately not being chased.

segments.name: Commercial Banking
segments.commentary: Grew 39% YoY and 8% QoQ to about INR35,300 Cr; transaction banking and forex income up 51% YoY.

segments.name: Inclusive Banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Grew 23% YoY and 6% QoQ; collection efficiency stable at 99.6%; 99% of book covered under CGFMU guarantee.

segments.name: Digital unsecured / personal loans
segments.commentary: Digital unsecured book up 23% YoY and 14% QoQ; personal loans up 81% YoY and 31% QoQ off a low base; credit card book grew marginally with 1.5 lakh new cards.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost guidance of close to 90 bps retained; H1 credit cost about 73-74 bps (81 bps including CGFMU premium); management does not expect to reach the guided range.
Long-term through-the-cycle credit cost of 90-100 bps.
Cost-to-assets ratio expected to improve YoY on a full-year basis; sequential improvement targeted over multiple years.
Deposit growth target around 25% YoY, linked to nominal GDP; loan growth target 2x-2.5x nominal GDP.
Mortgage growth expected to reach about 20% by next year.
Deposit pricing to stay at a 80-100 bps premium to mid-sized banks' term deposit rates.
25 bps repo hike to transmit to the ~30% floating-rate advances book over 3-4 months; full impact next quarter.
Insurance fee consultation paper will be a medium-term headwind to ROA; offsets cited include forex, credit cards, trade finance and UPI MDR income.
capex_capacity: Added 45 new deposit branches and 100+ asset centres in Q2.
Added about 2,400 employees, largely in customer-facing roles.
New Mumbai corporate office inaugurated in October 2026; senior leadership to co-locate in the next few months.
Agentic AI LOS for gold loans has disbursed over 2,500 loans across 40 branches; plans to extend to wheels, mortgages and commercial loans.
Cross Lead Platform with Voice AI enabled about 5% of Q2 disbursements; about 50% operating cost savings on that automated coverage.
Scorecard-led underwriting delivered INR500 Cr+ of unsecured disbursements in Q2.
demand_pricing: Disbursements up 33% YoY in Q2, broad-based across businesses.
Bank did not meaningfully participate in FCNR inflows (about US$230 million gross FCNR raised in Q2) due to limited overseas footprint.
Loan book is about 30% floating and 70% fixed rate; commercial banking book is almost entirely floating.
Management said wholesale deposit rates were cut, while retail deposit rates have not fallen in line with the 125 bps repo cuts.
Gold loan growth moderating industry-wide as lower gold prices reduce renewals and top-ups.
Wheels festive demand described as strong; Diwali expected to add to demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is deposit growth one-off or sustainable, and what is the sustainable deposit and CASA growth rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth reflects distribution and technology investments, not one-offs; CA balances up about 60% on daily average. Target is around 25% YoY deposit growth linked to nominal GDP, though the 29% print may be above plan.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank keep an 80-100 bps term deposit premium to other banks if rates rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will keep the 80-100 bps premium strategy and cost of funds is pegged to mid-sized banks; it will react if they do.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for asset quality, El Nino and drought, and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Six-month credit cost is about 73-74 bps (81 bps with CGFMU premium) vs guidance of about 90 bps; SMA and collection efficiency reported as robust through September with no stress seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Slippages rose QoQ in Q2; which segments drove it and is it a trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ is not comparable due to seasonality from semi-annual tractor billing in June and December, which affects roughly 12-13% of the wheels book; YoY trend is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: How will the insurance fee headwind (about 7-8 bps of ROA) be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged a medium-term headwind; offsets include forex, credit card, trade finance and UPI MDR income, plus cost-to-assets improvement and lower cost of funds.

qa_highlights.question: What are gold loan slowdown, LTV and margin trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY growth is over 100% off a small base; QoQ moderation is due to lower gold prices, portfolio LTV is about 75% and unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for mortgages and wheels growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Wheels growing 27-28% YoY with strong festive demand; mortgages growing 10-12% in core markets and targeted to reach about 20% next year; Southern mortgage book from Fincare is being rebuilt.

risks_watch: Deposit competition and rising rates may cap further cost-of-funds improvement and compress NIM, given the 70% fixed-rate advances book.
Insurance fee consultation paper could lower fee income and weigh on ROA in the medium term.
Drought in Central India, high oil prices and El Nino could hit asset quality in Q3; management said Q4 is not expected to show surprises.
October collection efficiency not yet disclosed; management said there was no impact up to 30 September.
PCR declined; management says provisioning is policy-driven, not target-driven.
Southern mortgage book rebuild post Fincare integration may take time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, deposits and asset quality, with a measured tone on NIM and rate-cycle risks. Management was evasive on specific data requests (savings and term deposit cost, CGFMU premium, October collections, mortgage slippage figures), citing non-disclosure.
key_quotes: Our deposits grew strongly by 29% YoY and 8% QoQ (vs banking system growth of 18% yoY).
I don't think there is any one-off there.
So my deposit franchise will improve, which should help me lower the cost of funds differential versus other peer mid-sized banks over a medium-term outlook.
If they react, we will necessarily be forced to react, given the platform disadvantage that we currently have.
